problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}y\,dx+x\,dy,$ where $C$ is a portion of the ellipse parametrized by $r(t)=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [\frac{\pi }{12},\frac{\pi }{4}].$

activity_context.topic_title: Sums of Line Integrals With Respect to X and Y Over Parametric Curves

examples.problem: Evaluate $\displaystyle \int\limits_C y\,\mathrm{d}x -x\,\mathrm{d}y ,$ where $C$ is a portion of the ellipse parametrized by $\mathbf{r}(t)=\cos t\,\mathbf{i} + 3\sin t\,\mathbf{j}$ for $t\in[0,\pi].$
examples.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t) = \cos t, \qquad
y(t) = 3\sin t.
$$

The derivative of $\mathbf r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}y\,dx-x\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }y\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt-x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(y\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot 3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }-3{sin}^{2}⁡t-3{cos}^{2}⁡t\,dt \\  & =-3{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t\,dt \\  & =-3{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\,dt \\  & =-3{t|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-3\pi \end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}{y}^{2}\,dx+x\,dy+z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the line $r(t)=t\,i+2t\,j+3t\,k$ for $t\in [0,5]?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=t,\,y(t)=2t,\,z(t)=3t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t)\,k \\  & =\,i+2\,j+3\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}{y}^{2}\,dx+x\,dy+z\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{5}{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}({y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}4{t}^{2}\cdot (1)+t\cdot (2)+3t\cdot (3)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}4{t}^{2}+11t\,dt\end{aligned}
$$
